entries.4e31709c90f4e624a5b707aeb766604b62b07283: <div sID="gen8919" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="12" osisID="Neh.12" sID="Neh.12"/> <div eID="gen8919" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8920" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen8921" type="x-p"/> In this chapter are preserved upon record, I. The names of the chief of the priests and the Levites that came up with Zerubbabel, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.1-Neh.12.9">ver. 1-9</reference>. II. The succession of the high priests, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.10-Neh.12.11">ver. 10, 11</reference>. III. The names of the next generation of the other chief priests, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.12-Neh.12.21">ver. 12-21</reference>. IV. The eminent Levites that were in Nehemiah's time, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.22-Neh.12.26">ver. 22-26</reference>. V. The solemnity of dedicating the wall of Jerusalem, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.27-Neh.12.43">ver. 27-43</reference>. VI. The settling of the offices of the priests and Levites in the temple, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.44-Neh.12.47">ver. 44-47</reference>.
entries.000e47c1c71d2f55f0b2dc36ba9e90901fea9994: <div eID="gen8921" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen8920" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Priests and Levites That Returned. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 444.)</title> <div sID="gen8922" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> Now these <hi type="italic">are</hi> the priests and the Levites that went up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra, <hi type="super">2</hi> Amariah, Malluch, Hattush, <hi type="super">3</hi> Shechaniah, Rehum, Meremoth, <hi type="super">4</hi> Iddo, Ginnetho, Abijah, <hi type="super">5</hi> Miamin, Maadiah, Bilgah, <hi type="super">6</hi> Shemaiah, and Joiarib, Jedaiah, <hi type="super">7</hi> Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These <hi type="italic">were</hi> the chief of the priests and of their brethren in the days of Jeshua. <hi type="super">8</hi> Moreover the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, <hi type="italic">and</hi> Mattaniah, <hi type="italic">which was</hi> over the thanksgiving, he and his brethren. <hi type="super">9</hi> Also Bakbukiah and Unni, their brethren, <hi type="italic">were</hi> over against them in the watches. <hi type="super">10</hi> And Jeshua begat Joiakim, Joiakim also begat Eliashib, and Eliashib begat Joiada, <hi type="super">11</hi> And Joiada begat Jonathan, and Jonathan begat Jaddua. <hi type="super">12</hi> And in the days of Joiakim were priests, the chief of the fathers: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah; <hi type="super">13</hi> Of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan; <hi type="super">14</hi> Of Melicu, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph; <hi type="super">15</hi> Of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai; <hi type="super">16</hi> Of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam; <hi type="super">17</hi> Of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai; <hi type="super">18</hi> Of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan; <hi type="super">19</hi> And of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi; <hi type="super">20</hi> Of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber; <hi type="super">21</hi> Of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethaneel. <hi type="super">22</hi> The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, and Johanan, and Jaddua, <hi type="italic">were</hi> recorded chief of the fathers: also the priests, to the reign of Darius the Persian. <hi type="super">23</hi> The sons of Levi, the chief of the fathers, <hi type="italic">were</hi> written in the book of the chronicles, even until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib. <hi type="super">24</hi> And the chief of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with their brethren over against them, to praise <hi type="italic">and</hi> to give thanks, according to the commandment of David the man of God, ward over against ward. <hi type="super">25</hi> Mattaniah, and Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, Akkub, <hi type="italic">were</hi> porters keeping the ward at the thresholds of the gates. <hi type="super">26</hi> These <hi type="italic">were</hi> in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest, the scribe. <div eID="gen8922" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8923" type="x-p"/> We have here the names, and little more than the names, of a great many priests and Levites, that were eminent in their day among the returned Jews. Why this register should be here inserted by Nehemiah does not appear, perhaps to keep in remembrance those good men, that posterity might know to whom they were beholden, under God, for the happy revival and re-establishment of their religion among them. Thus must we contribute towards the performance of that promise, <reference osisRef="Ps.112.6">Ps. cxii. 6</reference>, <hi type="italic">The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance.</hi> Let the memory of the just be blessed, be perpetuated. It is a debt we still owe to faithful ministers to <hi type="italic">remember our guides,</hi> who have <hi type="italic">spoken to us the word of God,</hi> <reference osisRef="Heb.13.7">Heb. xiii. 7</reference>. Perhaps it is intended to stir up their posterity, who succeeded them in the priest's office and inherited their dignities and preferments, to imitate their courage and fidelity. It is good to know what our godly ancestors and predecessors were, that we may learn thereby what we should be. We have here, 1. The names of the priests and Levites that came up with the first out of Babylon, when Jeshua was high priest. Jeremiah and Ezra are mentioned with the first (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.1">v. 1</reference>), but, it is supposed, not Jeremiah the prophet nor Ezra the scribe; the fame of the one was long before and that of the other some time after, though both of them were priests. Of one of the Levites it is said (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.8">v. 8</reference>) that he was <hi type="italic">over the thanksgiving,</hi> that is, he was entrusted to see that the psalms, the thanksgiving psalms, were constantly sung in the temple in due time and manner. The Levites kept their turns in their watches, reliving one another as becomes brethren, fellow-labourers, and fellow-soldiers. 2. The succession of high priests during the Persian monarchy, from Jeshua (or Jesus), who was high priest at the time of the restoration, to Jaddua (or Jaddus), who was high priest when Alexander the Great, after the conquest of Tyre, came to Jerusalem, and paid great respect to this Jaddus, who met him in his pontifical habit, and showed him the prophecy of Daniel, which foretold his conquests. 3. The next generation of priests, who were chief men, and active in the days of Joiakim, sons of the first set. Note, We have reason to acknowledge God's favour to his church, and care of it, in that, as one generation of ministers passes away, another comes. All those who are mentioned <reference osisRef="Neh.12.1-Neh.12.11">v. 1</reference>, &c., as eminent in their generation, are again mentioned, though with some variation in several of the names, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.12-Neh.12.24">v. 12</reference>, &c., except two, as having sons that were likewise eminent in their generation—a rare instance, that twenty good fathers should leave behind them twenty good sons (for so many here are) that filled up their places. 4. The next generation of Levites, or rather a latter generation; for those priests who are mentioned flourished in the days of Joiakim the high priest, these Levites in the days of Eliashib, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.22">v. 22</reference>. Perhaps <hi type="italic">then</hi> the forementioned families of the priests began to degenerate, and the third generation of them came short of the first two; but the work of God shall never fail for want of instruments. Then a generation of Levites was <hi type="italic">raised up,</hi> who were <hi type="italic">recorded chief of the fathers</hi> (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.22">v. 22</reference>), and were eminently serviceable to the interests of the church, and their service not the less acceptable either to God or to his people for their being Levites only, of the lower rank of ministers. Eliashib the high priest being allied to Tobiah (<reference osisRef="Neh.13.4">ch. xiii. 4</reference>), the other priests grew remiss; but then the Levites appeared the more zealous, as appears by this, that those who were now employed in expounding (<reference osisRef="Neh.8.7">ch. viii. 7</reference>) and in praying (<reference osisRef="Neh.9.4-Neh.9.5">ch. ix. 4, 5</reference>) were all Levites, not priests, regard being had to their personal qualifications more than to their order. These Levites were some of them singers (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.24">v. 24</reference>), <hi type="italic">to praise and give thanks,</hi> others of them porters (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.25">v. 25</reference>), <hi type="italic">keeping the ward at the thresholds of the gates, and both according to the command of David.</hi>
entries.53e2e30820bcf45cfd4a21309049ac963d0ade70: <div eID="gen8923" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Dedication of the Wall. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 444.)</title> <div sID="gen8924" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">27</hi> And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites out of all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem, to keep the dedication with gladness, both with thanksgivings, and with singing, <hi type="italic">with</hi> cymbals, psalteries, and with harps. <hi type="super">28</hi> And the sons of the singers gathered themselves together, both out of the plain country round about Jerusalem, and from the villages of Netophathi; <hi type="super">29</hi> Also from the house of Gilgal, and out of the fields of Geba and Azmaveth: for the singers had builded them villages round about Jerusalem. <hi type="super">30</hi> And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and purified the people, and the gates, and the wall. <hi type="super">31</hi> Then I brought up the princes of Judah upon the wall, and appointed two great <hi type="italic">companies of them that gave</hi> thanks, <hi type="italic">whereof one</hi> went on the right hand upon the wall toward the dung gate: <hi type="super">32</hi> And after them went Hoshaiah, and half of the princes of Judah, <hi type="super">33</hi> And Azariah, Ezra, and Meshullam, <hi type="super">34</hi> Judah, and Benjamin, and Shemaiah, and Jeremiah, <hi type="super">35</hi> And <hi type="italic">certain</hi> of the priests' sons with trumpets; <hi type="italic">namely,</hi> Zechariah the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Michaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph: <hi type="super">36</hi> And his brethren, Shemaiah, and Azarael, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethaneel, and Judah, Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God, and Ezra the scribe before them. <hi type="super">37</hi> And at the fountain gate, which was over against them, they went up by the stairs of the city of David, at the going up of the wall, above the house of David, even unto the water gate eastward. <hi type="super">38</hi> And the other <hi type="italic">company of them that gave</hi> thanks went over against <hi type="italic">them,</hi> and I after them, and the half of the people upon the wall, from beyond the tower of the furnaces even unto the broad wall; <hi type="super">39</hi> And from above the gate of Ephraim, and above the old gate, and above the fish gate, and the tower of Hananeel, and the tower of Meah, even unto the sheep gate: and they stood still in the prison gate. <hi type="super">40</hi> So stood the two <hi type="italic">companies of them that gave</hi> thanks in the house of God, and I, and the half of the rulers with me: <hi type="super">41</hi> And the priests; Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Michaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, <hi type="italic">and</hi> Hananiah, with trumpets; <hi type="super">42</hi> And Maaseiah, and Shemaiah, and Eleazar, and Uzzi, and Jehohanan, and Malchijah, and Elam, and Ezer. And the singers sang loud, with Jezrahiah <hi type="italic">their</hi> overseer. <hi type="super">43</hi> Also that day they offered great sacrifices, and rejoiced: for God had made them rejoice with great joy: the wives also and the children rejoiced: so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard even afar off. <div eID="gen8924" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8925" type="x-p"/> We have read of the building of the wall of Jerusalem with a great deal of fear and trembling; we have here an account of the dedicating of it with a great deal of joy and triumph. <hi type="italic">Those that sow in tears shall</hi> thus <hi type="italic">reap.</hi> <div eID="gen8925" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8926" type="x-p"/> I. We must enquire what was the meaning of this dedication of the wall; we will suppose it to include the dedication of the city too (<hi type="italic">continens pro contento—the thing containing for the thing contained</hi>), and therefore it was not done till the city was pretty well replenished, <reference osisRef="Neh.11.1">ch. xi. 1</reference>. It was a solemn thanksgiving to God for his great mercy to them in the perfecting of this undertaking, of which they were the more sensible because of the difficulty and opposition they had met with in it. 2. They hereby devoted the city in a peculiar manner to God and to his honour, and took possession of it for him and in his name. All our cities, all our houses, must have holiness to the Lord written upon them; but this city was (so as never any other was) a <hi type="italic">holy city,</hi> the <hi type="italic">city of the great King</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.48.2">Ps. xlviii. 2</reference> and <reference osisRef="Matt.5.35">Matt. v. 35</reference>): it had been so ever since God chose it to put his name there, and as such, it being now refitted, it was afresh dedicated to God by the builders and inhabitants, in token of their acknowledgment that they were his tenants, and their desire that it might still be his and that the property of it might never be altered. Whatever is done for their safety, ease, and comfort, must be designed for God's honour and glory. 3. They hereby put the city and its walls under the divine protection, owning that <hi type="italic">unless the Lord kept the city</hi> the walls were <hi type="italic">built in vain.</hi> When this city was in possession of the Jebusites, they committed the guardianship of it to their gods, though they were blind and lame ones, <reference osisRef="2Sam.5.6">2 Sam. v. 6</reference>. With much more reason do the people of God commit it to his keeping who is all-wise and almighty. The superstitious founders of cities had an eye to the lucky position of the heavens (see Mr. Gregory's works, p. 29, &c.); but these pious founders had an eye to God only, to his providence, and not to fortune. <div eID="gen8926" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8927" type="x-p"/> II. We must observe with what solemnity it was performed, under the direction of <reference osisRef="Neh.1">Nehemiah. 1</reference>. The Levites from all parts of the country were summoned to attend. The city must be dedicated to God, and therefore his ministers must be employed in the dedicating of it, and the surrender must pass through their hands. When those solemn feasts were over (<reference osisRef="Neh.8.1-Neh.9.38">ch. viii. and ix.</reference>) they went home to their respective posts, to mind their cures in the country; but now their presence and assistance were again called for. 2. Pursuant to this summons, there was a general rendezvous of all the Levites, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.28-Neh.12.29">v. 28, 29</reference>. Observe in what method they proceeded. (1.) They <hi type="italic">purified themselves,</hi> <reference osisRef="Neh.12.30">v. 30</reference>. We are concerned to <hi type="italic">cleanse our hands,</hi> and <hi type="italic">purify our hearts,</hi> when any work for God is to pass through them. They purified themselves and then the people. Those that would be instrumental to sanctify others must sanctify themselves, and set themselves apart for God, with purity of mind and sincerity of intention. Then they purified <hi type="italic">the gates and the wall.</hi> Then may we expect comfort when we are prepared to receive it. <hi type="italic">To the pure all things are pure</hi> (<reference osisRef="Titus.1.15">Tit. i. 15</reference>); and, to those who are sanctified, houses and tables, and all their creature comforts and enjoyments, are sanctified, <reference osisRef="1Tim.4.4-1Tim.4.5">1 Tim. iv. 4, 5</reference>. This purification was performed, it is probable, by sprinkling the <hi type="italic">water of purifying</hi> (or of <hi type="italic">separation,</hi> as it is called, <reference osisRef="Num.19.9">Num. xix. 9</reference>) on <hi type="italic">themselves</hi> and the <hi type="italic">people,</hi> the walls and the gates—a type of the blood of Christ, with which our consciences being <hi type="italic">purged from dead works,</hi> we become fit to <hi type="italic">serve the living God</hi> (<reference osisRef="Heb.9.14">Heb. ix. 14</reference>) and to be his care. (2.) The princes, priests, and Levites, walked round upon the wall in two companies, with musical instruments, to signify the dedication of it all to God, the whole circuit of it (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.36">v. 36</reference>); so that it is likely they sung psalms as they went along, to the praise and glory of God. This procession is here largely described. They had a rendezvous at one certain lace, where they divided themselves into two companies. Half of the princes, with several priests and Levites, went on the right hand, Ezra leading their van, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.36">v. 36</reference>. The other half of the princes and priests, who gave thanks likewise, went to the left hand, Nehemiah bringing up the rear, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.38">v. 38</reference>. At length both companies met in the temple, where they joined their thanksgivings, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.40">v. 40</reference>. The crowd of people, it is likely, walked on the ground, some within the wall and others without, one end of this ceremony being to affect them with the mercy they were giving thanks for, and to perpetuate the remembrance of it among them. Processions, for such purposes, have their use. (3.) The people <hi type="italic">greatly rejoiced,</hi> <reference osisRef="Neh.12.43">v. 43</reference>. While the princes, priests, and Levites, testified their joy and thankfulness by <hi type="italic">great sacrifices, sound of trumpet, musical instruments, and songs of praise,</hi> the common people testified theirs by loud shouts, which were heard afar off, further than the more harmonious sound of their songs and music: and these shouts, coming from a sincere and hearty joy, are here taken notice of; for God overlooks not, but graciously accepts, the honest zealous services of mean people, though there is in them little of art and they are far from being fine. It is observed that <hi type="italic">the women and children rejoiced;</hi> and their hosannas were not despised, but recorded to their praise. All that share in public mercies ought to join in public thanksgivings. The reason given is that <hi type="italic">God had made them rejoice with great joy.</hi> He had given them both matter for joy and hearts to rejoice; his providence had made them safe and easy, and then his grace made them cheerful and thankful. The baffled opposition of their enemies, no doubt, added to their joy and mixed triumph with it. Great mercies call for the most solemn returns of praise, <hi type="italic">in the courts of the Lord's house, in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem!</hi>
entries.ebcfa16d910b251a24f13eff5beb86b83622a614: <div eID="gen8927" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The People's Attention to Their Duty. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 444.)</title> <div sID="gen8928" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">44</hi> And at that time were some appointed over the chambers for the treasures, for the offerings, for the firstfruits, and for the tithes, to gather into them out of the fields of the cities the portions of the law for the priests and Levites: for Judah rejoiced for the priests and for the Levites that waited. <hi type="super">45</hi> And both the singers and the porters kept the ward of their God, and the ward of the purification, according to the commandment of David, <hi type="italic">and</hi> of Solomon his son. <hi type="super">46</hi> For in the days of David and Asaph of old <hi type="italic">there were</hi> chief of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving unto God. <hi type="super">47</hi> And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel, and in the days of Nehemiah, gave the portions of the singers and the porters, every day his portion: and they sanctified <hi type="italic">holy things</hi> unto the Levites; and the Levites sanctified <hi type="italic">them</hi> unto the children of Aaron. <div eID="gen8928" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8929" type="x-p"/> We have here an account of the remaining good effects of the universal joy that was at the dedication of the wall. When the solemnities of a thanksgiving day leave such impressions on ministers and people as that both are more careful and cheerful in doing their duty afterwards, then they are indeed acceptable to God and turn to a good account. So it was here. 1. The ministers were more careful than they had been of their work; the respect the people paid them upon this occasion encouraged them to diligence and watchfulness, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.45">v. 45</reference>. <hi type="italic">The singers kept the ward of their God,</hi> attending in due time to the duty of their office; the <hi type="italic">porters,</hi> too, <hi type="italic">kept the ward of the purification,</hi> that is, they took care to preserve the purity of the temple by denying admission to those that were ceremonially unclean. When the joy of the Lord thus engages us to our duty, and enlarges us in it, it is then an earnest of that joy which, in concurrence with the perfection of holiness, will be our everlasting bliss. 2. The people were more careful than they had been of the maintenance of their ministers. The people, at the dedication of the wall, among other things which they made matter of their joy, rejoiced <hi type="italic">for the priests and for the Levites that waited,</hi> <reference osisRef="Neh.12.44">v. 44</reference>. They had a great deal of comfort in their ministers, and were glad of them. When they observed how diligently they waited, and what pains they took in their work, they rejoiced in them. Note, The surest way for ministers to recommend themselves to their people, and gain an interest in their affections, is <hi type="italic">to wait on their ministry</hi> (<reference osisRef="Rom.12.7">Rom. xii. 7</reference>), to be humble and industrious, and to mind their business. When these did so the people thought nothing too much to do for them, to encourage them. The law had provided then <hi type="italic">their portions</hi> (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.44">v. 44</reference>), but what the better were they for that provision if what the law appointed them either was not duly collected or not justly paid to them? Now, (1.) Care is here taken for the collecting of their dues. They were modest, and would rather lose their right than call for it themselves. The people were many of them careless and would not bring their dues unless they were called upon; and therefore <hi type="italic">some were appointed</hi> whose office it should be to gather into the treasuries, <hi type="italic">out of the fields of the cities, the portions of the law for the priests and Levites</hi> (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.44">v. 44</reference>), that their portion might not be lost for want of being demanded. This is a piece of good service both to ministers and people, that the one may not come short of their maintenance nor the other of their duty. (2.) Care is taken that, being <hi type="italic">gathered in,</hi> they might be duly <hi type="italic">paid out,</hi> <reference osisRef="Neh.12.47">v. 47</reference>. They gave the singers and porters their daily portion, over and above what was due to them as Levites; for we may suppose that when David and Solomon appointed them their work (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.45-Neh.12.46">v. 45, 46</reference>), above what was required from them as Levites, they settled a fund for their further encouragement. Let those that labour more abundantly in the word and doctrine be counted worthy of this double honour. As for the other Levites, the tithes, here called <hi type="italic">the holy things,</hi> were duly set apart for them, out of which they paid the priests their tithe according to the law. Both are said to be <hi type="italic">sanctified;</hi> when what is contributed, either voluntarily or by law, for the support of religion and the maintenance of the ministry, is given with an eye to God and his honour, it is sanctified, and shall be accepted of him accordingly, and it will <hi type="italic">cause the blessing to rest on the house</hi> and all that is in it, <reference osisRef="Ezek.44.30">Ezek. xliv. 30</reference>.  <chapter eID="Neh.12"/> <div eID="gen8929" type="x-p"/>

entries.50b3a5ccad4206b1cb77d4f47bda44d87ad65007: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4378"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 12</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Neh.12.1-Neh.12.9">Ne 12:1-9</reference>. Priests and Levites Who Came Up with Zerubbabel.</title> <div sID="gen6340" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4378"/><hi type="bold">1. these are the priests--</hi>according to <reference osisRef="Neh.12.7">Ne 12:7</reference>, "the chief of the priests," the heads of the twenty-four courses into which the priesthood was divided (<reference osisRef="1Chr.24.1-1Chr.24.20">1Ch 24:1-20</reference>). Only four of the courses returned from the captivity (<reference osisRef="Neh.7.39-Neh.7.42">Ne 7:39-42</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezra.2.36-Ezra.2.39">Ezr 2:36-39</reference>). But these were divided by Zerubbabel, or Jeshua, into the original number of twenty-four. Twenty-two only are enumerated here, and no more than twenty in <reference osisRef="Neh.12.12-Neh.12.21">Ne 12:12-21</reference>. The discrepancy is due to the extremely probable circumstance that two of the twenty-four courses had become extinct in Babylon; for none belonging to them are reported as having returned (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.2-Neh.12.5">Ne 12:2-5</reference>). Hattush and Maadiah may be omitted in the account of those persons' families (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.12">Ne 12:12</reference>), for these had no sons.<div eID="gen6340" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6341" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Shealtiel--</hi>or Salathiel.<div eID="gen6341" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6342" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Ezra--</hi>This was most likely a different person from the pious and patriotic leader. If he were the same person, he would now have reached a very patriarchal age--and this longevity would doubtless be due to his eminent piety and temperance, which are greatly conducive to the prolongation of life, but, above all, to the special blessing of God, who had preserved and strengthened him for the accomplishment of the important work he was called upon to undertake in that critical period of the Church's history. <div eID="gen6342" type="x-p"/>
entries.75b722af89d23f2426f086a08305346f337aebd5: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4379"/><div sID="gen6343" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4379"/><hi type="bold">4. Abijah--</hi>one of the ancestors of John the Baptist (<reference osisRef="Luke.1.5">Lu 1:5</reference>). <div eID="gen6343" type="x-p"/>
entries.5a36fb082d6cb57d7f7fe2641aba8e9be496bb6d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4380"/><div sID="gen6344" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4380"/><hi type="bold">9. their brethren, were over against them in the watches--</hi>that is, according to some, their stations--the places where they stood when officiating--"ward over against ward" (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.24">Ne 12:24</reference>); or, according to others, in alternate watches, in course of rotation. <div eID="gen6344" type="x-p"/>
entries.0cd7d625c7bd4c2c4e57d71e2a7e098afded1be5: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4381"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Neh.12.10-Neh.12.47">Ne 12:10-47</reference>. Succession of the High Priests.</title> <div sID="gen6345" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4381"/><hi type="bold">10. Jeshua begat Joiakim, &c.--</hi>This enumeration was of great importance, not only as establishing their individual purity of descent, but because the chronology of the Jews was henceforth to be reckoned, not as formerly by the reigns of their kings, but by the successions of their high priests. <div eID="gen6345" type="x-p"/>
entries.b772d31fa9a785e58ff2964ce66dfbc1d1ca10b1: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4382"/><div sID="gen6346" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4382"/><hi type="bold">11. Jaddua--</hi>It is an opinion entertained by many commentators that this person was the high priest whose dignified appearance, solemn manner, and splendid costume overawed and interested so strongly the proud mind of Alexander the Great; and if he were not this person (as some object that this Jaddua was not in office till a considerable period after the death of Nehemiah), it might probably be his father, called by the same name. <div eID="gen6346" type="x-p"/>
entries.f42fb9c29c77e14c87915bb0f56282f7a328c090: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4383"/><div sID="gen6347" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4383"/><hi type="bold">12. in the days of Joiakim were priests, the chief of the fathers--</hi>As there had been priests in the days of Jeshua, so in the time of Joiakim, the son and successor of Jeshua, the sons of those persons filled the priestly office in the place of their fathers, some of whom were still alive, though many were dead. <div eID="gen6347" type="x-p"/>
entries.472eb8fb0e6c648fde7e0766a8782058a2de642b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4384"/><div sID="gen6348" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4384"/><hi type="bold">23. The sons of Levi ... were written in the book of the chronicles--</hi>that is, the public registers in which the genealogies were kept with great regularity and exactness. <div eID="gen6348" type="x-p"/>
entries.11999ebb1f18dedb50ee5d5c04b7ba4892ee42c4: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4385"/><div sID="gen6349" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4385"/><hi type="bold">27-43. at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem--</hi>This ceremony of consecrating the wall and gates of the city was an act of piety on the part of Nehemiah, not merely to thank God in a general way for having been enabled to bring the building to a happy completion, but especially because that city was the place which He had chosen. It also contained the temple which was hallowed by the manifestation of His presence, and anew set apart to His service. It was on these accounts that Jerusalem was called "the holy city," and by this public and solemn act of religious observance, after a long period of neglect and desecration, it was, as it were, restored to its rightful proprietor. The dedication consisted in a solemn ceremonial, in which the leading authorities, accompanied by the Levitical singers, summoned from all parts of the country, and by a vast concourse of people, marched in imposing procession round the city walls, and, pausing at intervals to engage in united praises, prayer, and sacrifices, supplicated the continued presence, favor, and blessing on "the holy city." "The assembly convened near Jaffa Gate, where the procession commences. Then (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.31">Ne 12:31</reference>) I brought up the princes of Judah upon the wall (near the Valley Gate), and appointed two great companies of them that gave thanks, whereof one went on the right hand upon the wall towards the dung gate (through Bethzo). And after them went Hoshaiah, and half of the princes of Judah. And (<reference osisRef="Neh.12.37">Ne 12:37</reference>) at the fountain gate, which was over against them, they (descending by the Tower of Siloam on the interior, and then reascending) went up by the stairs of the city of David, at the going up of the wall, above the house of David, even unto the water gate eastward (by the staircase of the rampart, having descended to dedicate the fountain structures). And the other company of them that gave thanks went over against them (both parties having started from the junction of the first and second walls), and I after them, and the half of the people upon the wall, from beyond the tower of the furnaces even unto the broad wall (beyond the corner gate). And from above the gate of Ephraim, and above the old gate (and the gate of Benjamin), and above the fish gate, and the tower of Hananeel, and the tower of Meah, even unto the sheep gate; and they stood still in the prison gate (or high gate, at the east end of the bridge). So stood the two companies of them that gave thanks in the house of God, and I, and half of the rulers with me (having thus performed the circuit of the investing walls), and arrived in the courts of the temple" [Barclay, City of the Great King]. <div eID="gen6349" type="x-p"/>
entries.0566139e0c2aa563da1b18765e5ef5a338d802a0: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4387"/><div sID="gen6351" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4387"/><hi type="bold">44. portions of the law--</hi>that is, "prescribed by the law."<div eID="gen6351" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6352" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">for Judah rejoiced for the priests and ... Levites that waited--</hi>The cause of this general satisfaction was either the full restoration of the temple service and the reorganized provision for the permanent support of the ministry, or it was the pious character and eminent gifts of the guardians of religion. <div eID="gen6352" type="x-p"/>
entries.6bb109a5a008179b806e944fe90dc271cf35565c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4388"/><div sID="gen6353" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4388"/><hi type="bold">45. the singers and the porters kept ... the ward of the purification--</hi>that is, took care that no unclean person was allowed to enter within the precincts of the sacred building. This was the official duty of the porters (<reference osisRef="2Chr.23.19">2Ch 23:19</reference>), with whom, owing to the pressure of circumstances, it was deemed expedient that the singers should be associated as assistants. <div eID="gen6353" type="x-p"/>
entries.8a3ff090ea1e3e8c2201b5e99ef0ad98d0531318: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4389"/><div sID="gen6354" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4389"/><hi type="bold">47. all Israel ... sanctified holy things unto the Levites,--</hi>&c. The people, selecting the tithes and first-fruits, devoted them to the use of the Levites, to whom they belonged by appointment of the law. The Levites acted in the same way with the tithes due from them to the priests. Thus all classes of the people displayed a conscientious fidelity in paying the dues to the temple and the servants of God who were appointed to minister in it. <chapter eID="Neh.12"/>

entries.46f489c5a991f6df445f44b96a491dfdbd0a291a: <div eID="gen15286" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen15287" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen15288" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen15288" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen15287" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen15289" type="x-p"/> Account of the priests and Levites that come up with Zerubbabel, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.1-Neh.12.7">Neh 12:1-7</reference>. Of the Levites, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.8-Neh.12.21">Neh 12:8-21</reference>. The Levites in the days of Eliashib, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.22-Neh.12.26">Neh 12:22-26</reference>. Of the dedication of the wall, and its ceremonies, vv. 27-43. Different officers appointed, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.44-Neh.12.47">Neh 12:44-47</reference>. <div eID="gen15289" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15290" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen15290" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15291" type="x-p"/> Now these are the priests - Not the whole, but the chief of them, as we are informed, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.7">Neh 12:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.22">Neh 12:22</reference>, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.23">Neh 12:23</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Neh.12.24">Neh 12:24</reference>. The Septuagint omit <reference osisRef="Neh.12.3">Neh 12:3</reference>, except the word Shechaniah; as also <reference osisRef="Neh.12.4">Neh 12:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.5">Neh 12:5</reference>,<reference osisRef="Neh.12.6">Neh 12:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.9">Neh 12:9</reference>,<reference osisRef="Neh.12.37">Neh 12:37</reference>, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.38">Neh 12:38</reference>, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.39">Neh 12:39</reference>, <reference osisRef="Neh.12.40">Neh 12:40</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Neh.12.41">Neh 12:41</reference>. The Arabic omits the first twenty-six verses, and <reference osisRef="Neh.12.29">Neh 12:29</reference>. Mention is made of Ezra in this verse; and he is generally allowed to be that Ezra whose book the reader has already passed over, and who came to Jerusalem in the time of Cyrus, with Zerubbabel. If this were the same, he must have been at this time upward of a hundred years of age: and this case is not improbable, as an especial providence might preserve such a very useful man beyond the ordinary age of men. See what has been said on the case of Nehemiah, <reference osisRef="Neh.1.1">Neh 1:1</reference> (note).
entries.5bd93ac557a644f464bab995b848c350d882e8bf: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen15291" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15292" type="x-p"/> The chief of the priests - They were twenty-four orders or courses in number, all subordinate to each other; as established by David, <reference osisRef="1Chr.24.18">1Chr 24:18</reference>. And these orders or courses were continued till the destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans. See Calmet.
entries.17fa5e3a3c5bf5512b35e844dd8d01c44e5ba352: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen15292" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15293" type="x-p"/> Over the thanksgiving - The principal singers: See on <reference osisRef="Neh.11.17">Neh 11:17</reference> (note).
entries.c9baf271bd2b81688d01a4a314be739f5c2cb4bb: <hi type="bold">Verse 22</hi> <div eID="gen15293" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15294" type="x-p"/> Jaddua - This was probably the high priest who went in his pontifical robes, accompanied by his brethren, to meet Alexander the Great, when he was advancing towards Jerusalem, with the purpose to destroy it, after having conquered Tyre and Gaza. Alexander was so struck with the appearance of the priest, that he forbore all hostilities against Jerusalem, prostrated himself before Jaddua, worshipped the Lord at the temple, and granted many privileges to the Jews. See Josephus, Ant. lib. xi., c. 3, and Prideaux's Connections, lib. 7, p. 695. <div eID="gen15294" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15295" type="x-p"/> To the reign of Darius the Persian - Calmet maintains that this must have been Darius Codomanus, who was defeated by Alexander the Great: but Archbishop Usher understands it of Darius Nothus, in whose reign he thinks Jaddua was born, who was high priest under Darius Codomanus.
entries.1ba3ce5e174a618a92b327d3b7723f8a4de805cb: <hi type="bold">Verse 23</hi> <div eID="gen15295" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15296" type="x-p"/> The book of the chronicles - This is not the book of Chronicles which we have now, no such list being found in it; but some other book or register, which is lost.
entries.032e21f0cc9fa5578f35be8913bbe44cda3d4e26: <hi type="bold">Verse 25</hi> <div eID="gen15296" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15297" type="x-p"/> The thresholds of the gates - Some understand this of a sort of porticoes at the gates, and are puzzled about it, because they find no mention of porticoes elsewhere: but why may we not suppose these to resemble our watch-boxes or some temporary moveable shelters for those who took care of the gates? That there must have been some such conveniences, common sense dictates.
entries.e64e1af8bf10704001992cabf0afa984a91a09fe: <hi type="bold">Verse 27</hi> <div eID="gen15297" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15298" type="x-p"/> At the dedication of the wall - They sent for the Levites from all quarters, that this dedication might be as solemn and majestic as possible; and it is likely that this was done as soon as convenient after the walls were finished. The dedication seems to have consisted in processions of the most eminent persons around the walls, and thanksgivings to God, who had enabled them to bring the work to so happy a conclusion: and no doubt to all this were added a particular consecration of the city to God, and the most earnest invocation that he would take it under his guardian care, and defend it and its inhabitants against all their enemies. <div eID="gen15298" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15299" type="x-p"/> The ancients consecrated their cities to the gods, and the very walls were considered as sacred. Ovid gives us an account of the ceremonies used in laying the foundations of the walls of the city of Rome, by Romulus. After having consulted together who should give name to the city, and have the direction of the wall by which it was necessary to surround it, they agreed to let the case be decided by the flight of birds. One brother went to the top of the Mons Palatinus, the other to that of Mount Aventine. Romulus saw twelve birds, Remus saw but six; the former, therefore, according to agreement, took the command. The poet thus describes the ceremonies used on the occasion: - <div eID="gen15299" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15300" type="x-p"/> Apta dies legitur, qua moenia signet aratro; <div eID="gen15300" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15301" type="x-p"/> Sacra Palis suberant; inde movetur opus. <div eID="gen15301" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15302" type="x-p"/> Fossa fit ad solidum: fruges jaciuntur in ima. <div eID="gen15302" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15303" type="x-p"/> Et de vicino terra petita solo <div eID="gen15303" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15304" type="x-p"/> Fossa repletur humo, plenaeque imponitur ara; <div eID="gen15304" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15305" type="x-p"/> Et novus accenso finditur igne focus. <div eID="gen15305" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15306" type="x-p"/> Inde, premens stivam, designat moenia sulco; <div eID="gen15306" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15307" type="x-p"/> Alba jugum niveo cum bove vacca tulit. <div eID="gen15307" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15308" type="x-p"/> Vox tuit haec regis; Condenti Jupiter urbem, <div eID="gen15308" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15309" type="x-p"/> Et genitor Mavors, Vestaque mater ades: <div eID="gen15309" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15310" type="x-p"/> Quosque pium est adhibere deos, advertite cuncti: <div eID="gen15310" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15311" type="x-p"/> Auspicibus vobis hoc mihi surgat opus. <div eID="gen15311" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15312" type="x-p"/> Longa sit huic aetas, dominaeque potentia terrae: <div eID="gen15312" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15313" type="x-p"/> Sitque sub hac oriens occiduusque dies! Ille precabatur. <div eID="gen15313" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15314" type="x-p"/> Ovid, Fast. lib. iv., ver. 819. "A proper day is chosen in which he may mark out the walls with the plough: the festival of Pales was at hand when the work was begun. A ditch is dug down to the solid clay, into which they cast the fruits of the season; and bring earth from the neighboring ground, with which they fill up the trench; and on it build an altar, by whose flames the newly made hearth is cleft asunder. Then Romulus, seizing the plough, which a white heifer yoked with a snowy bull drew along, marked out the walls with a furrow. And thus spoke the king: 'O Jupiter, and Father Mars, with Matron Vesta, prosper me in founding this city! And all ye gods, approach, whomsoever it is right to invoke! Under your auspices may the work arise; may it endure for countless ages, and be the mistress of the world; and may the East and the West be under its control!' Thus he prayed." <div eID="gen15314" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15315" type="x-p"/> The above is a literal version, and the account is not a little curious.
entries.73ccb672cb59bd96f48e7abc4c2555166c189453: <hi type="bold">Verse 29</hi> <div eID="gen15315" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15316" type="x-p"/> From the house of Gilgal, and out of the fields of Geba and Azmaveth - Or, from Beth-Gilgal; a village erected in the place where the Israelites encamped after they had, under the direction of Joshua, passed over Jordan.
entries.e1708c24312440b017cdf270282c2c4c3164f21f: <hi type="bold">Verse 30</hi> <div eID="gen15316" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15317" type="x-p"/> The priests and the Levites purified themselves - This consisted in washings, abstinence from wine, and other matters, which, on all other occasions, were lawful. And as to the purifying of the gates and the walls, nothing was requisite but to remove all filth from the former, and all rubbish that might have been laid against the latter.
entries.65ba50e00a95dc97433b678cd0ef2b91282b4984: <hi type="bold">Verse 31</hi> <div eID="gen15317" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15318" type="x-p"/> Then I brought up the princes - Perhaps this verse should be read thus: "Then I caused the princes of Judah to go upon the wall, and appointed two great choirs, [to sing praises], and two processions, one on the right hand, etc. <div eID="gen15318" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15319" type="x-p"/> The following seems to have been the order of the procession: he divided the priests, the Levites, the magistrates, and the people into two companies; each company to go round one half of the wall. They began at the dung gate, one party going to the right and the other to the left, till they met at the great space opposite to the temple, where they all offered many sacrifices to God, and rejoiced with exceeding great joy; shouting so that the noise was heard a great way off.
entries.6580de89ad316a392a8d1a2d8582e499adac849d: <hi type="bold">Verse 38</hi> <div eID="gen15319" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15320" type="x-p"/> The broad wall - What part this was, we know not: it might have been a place designed for a public promenade, or a parade for assembling the troops or guard of the temple.
entries.3edb0a976ed80d21b2a831117e323cc73be46df6: <hi type="bold">Verse 47</hi> <div eID="gen15320" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15321" type="x-p"/> All Israel - gave the portions of the singers - The singers and the porters were supported by the people at large; and each of these had their portions served out to them daily. <div eID="gen15321" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15322" type="x-p"/> And they sanctified - unto the Levites - The things which were provided for sacred uses were delivered by the people to the Levites, and the Levites presented them to the priests. <div eID="gen15322" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15323" type="x-p"/> The children of Aaron - This may refer principally to the tithes which the people brought to the Levites; the tithe or tenth of which the Levites gave to the priests. The presenting these tithes is termed sanctifying them; that is, dedicating them to those sacred or ecclesiastical uses for which they were designed: this is a very general meaning of the word sanctify in Scripture.  <chapter eID="Neh.12"/> <div eID="gen15323" type="x-p"/>

entries.dfcb762735b031496b61df52361c86d33e546a90:
Lists of the orders of priests and Levites. - Neh 12:1-9 contain a list of the heads of the priests and Levites who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and Joshua. The high priests during five generations are next mentioned by name, Neh 12:10, Neh 12:11. Then follow the names of the heads of the priestly houses in the days of Joiakim the high priest; and finally, Neh 12:22-26, the names of the heads of the Levites at the same period, with titles and subscriptions.
Neh 12:1-7 Neh 12:1 contains the title of the first list, Neh 12:1-9. “These are the priests and Levites who went up with Zerubbabel ... and Joshua;” comp. Ezr 2:1-2. Then follow, Neh 12:1, the names of the priests, with the subscription: “These are the heads of the priests and of their brethren, in the days of Joshua.” ואחיהם still depends on ראשׁי. The brethren of the priests are the Levites, as being their fellow-tribesmen and assistants. Two-and-twenty names of such heads are enumerated, and these reappear, with but slight variations attributable to clerical errors, as names of priestly houses in Neh 12:12-21, where they are given in conjunction with the names of those priests who, in the days of Joiakim, either represented these houses, or occupied as heads the first position in them. The greater number, viz., 15, of these have already been mentioned as among those who, together with Nehemiah, sealed as heads of their respective houses the agreement to observe the law, Neh 10. Hence the present chapter appears to be the most appropriate place for comparing with each other the several statements given in the books of Nehemiah and Ezra, concerning the divisions or orders of priests in the period immediately following the return from the captivity, and for discussing the question how the heads and houses of priests enumerated in Neh 10 and 12 stand related on the one hand to the list of the priestly races who returned with Zerubbabel and Joshua, and on the other to the twenty-four orders of priests instituted by David. For the purpose of giving an intelligible answer to this question, we first place in juxtaposition the three lists given in Nehemiah, chs. 10 and 12.
